title: Set Apart to Be His Own

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You are to be holy to me because I, the LORD, am holy, and I have set you apart from the nations to be my own.'" - Lev 20:26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the summary of the whole chapter, and it lands on four words: to be my own.

That is the purpose behind every command in Leviticus 20. Not rules for their own sake. Not moral improvement as an end in itself. God was making a people who belonged to Him.

Read the verse again and notice the direction. Holy to me. I have set you apart. My own. Every phrase is relational. Holiness is not a standard to be achieved; it is the shape of a life that belongs to Someone.

That changes how we read a chapter like this. All the severity, all the boundaries, all the warnings — they exist because God was determined to have a people of His own who would not be destroyed by what destroyed everyone around them.

Paul writes that Christ gave himself for us to redeem us from all wickedness and to purify for himself a people that are his very own, eager to do what is good (Titus 2:14).

His very own. The same phrase, the same heart, fifteen centuries later.

You are not your own; you were bought at a price (1 Cor 6:19-20). That is not a burden. It is the deepest security a person can have.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of holiness as a standard or as belonging?
2. What does it mean to you that God wanted a people of His very own?
3. How does belonging to God change the way you face today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You wanted a people of Your own, and that in Christ I am one of them. Let my life show whose I am. Amen.
